## Family Stories

Albert George Telfer was the fifth child of John and Caroline Telfer, born on 14 November 1881 at Angle Farm, near Hawker. His birth came at a time when the family was establishing their home — a well had been sunk providing permanent water for stock and household use, and they were harvesting their fourth crop. In 1903, when his father purchased the Warcowie homestead, Albert took over its management, beginning a long farming career.

Albert was a farmer with a keen interest in examining new ideas and learning from them. He became a foundation member of the Warcowie Agricultural Bureau and took an active part in its activities. He married Beatrice Rowe, and their children — Rita Joyce, Beatrice Sylvia, Douglas Ivan, Melville Bruce, John Alick Ralph and Murray Keith — were all born while the family lived at Warcowie.

In 1923, Albert bought a farm at Hill River, six miles east of Clare, so that his children could attend the High School there. Farming at Clare, one of the wetter areas of the state, was very different from the drier conditions he had been accustomed to at Hawker. His first crop at Hill River was quite good, but 80 acres were destroyed by a severe hailstorm. Despite such setbacks, Albert and Beatrice built a new life at Clare, and their family grew and prospered there.

*(From the Borders to the Bush, pp.144–146)*
